name: dnsviz
desc: Tools for analyzing and visualizing DNS and DNSSEC behavior
why: Visualizing DNSSEC chains of trust is a great door into DNS internals that almost nobody looks at.

brief.what_it_is: DNSViz is a tool suite for analysing and visualising the Domain Name System, including its DNSSEC security extensions. It is driven from a single command-line tool, dnsviz, with subcommands that run in a pipeline. probe takes domain names and sends DNS queries to recursive or authoritative servers, writing the results as JSON. grok takes that JSON and assesses the named domains, and graph or print turn the assessment into an image, an interactive HTML page, or plain text. The README says the tool suite also powers the web analysis at dnsviz.net.
brief.why_it_exists: The README describes it as a tool suite for analysis and visualisation of DNS behaviour, including DNSSEC, and notes that it powers the Web-based analysis at dnsviz.net. It also documents pre-deployment testing, so operators can check a zone or its delegation before changes go live.
brief.how_it_works: probe records raw queries and responses as JSON, so the collection step is separate from analysis. grok then assesses the recorded data, and graph (Graphviz-based, per its dependencies) or print renders the result. The stages can be piped together, and the trust anchor can be supplied as a root or zone DNSKEY file to show authentication status. For pre-deployment work, the -x, -N and -D options supply zone files, server addresses, future delegation records or DS records, and the README says BIND's named is started to serve local zone files.

commands_seen.context: Probes example.com through the configured resolvers and saves the queries and responses as JSON.
Queries authoritative servers and follows delegations from the root, writing the results to a JSON file.
Assesses the recorded probe data at info level and writes the assessment to a JSON file.
Renders the analysis of example.com as a PNG graph image.
Produces an interactive HTML graph from saved probe results, with a filename derived from the domain.
Prints the textual analysis of saved probe results to the terminal.
Wrapper that combines probe and print in one step, with dig-like usage, using the first configured resolver.
Analyses example.com through a named recursive resolver, using a trust anchor file.

commands_seen.cmd: docker run --network host dnsviz/dnsviz probe -4 -A example.com > example.json
commands_seen.context: Runs authoritative probing inside the container on the host network, which the README recommends for authoritative queries.

brief.install_notes: Available from Debian, Ubuntu, Fedora, Gentoo and FreeBSD repositories, and from EPEL for RHEL and CentOS 8 and 9. On RHEL or CentOS Stream you must enable CodeReady Builder or PowerTools and EPEL before running sudo dnf install dnsviz. The README says Homebrew and MacPorts work on macOS. Dependencies are Python (2.7 or 3.5 to 3.12), dnspython 1.13.0 or later, pygraphviz 1.3 or later, which needs Graphviz, and cryptography 36.0.0 or later, which needs OpenSSL. For a virtualenv install, run pip install dnsviz after the dependencies. GOST algorithm support needs the OpenSSL GOST engine plus M2Crypto. Pre-deployment tests with zone files need ISC BIND. Debian's AppArmor profile for named can block this, and the README gives sudo apparmor_parser -R /etc/apparmor.d/usr.sbin.named as a temporary workaround.
brief.standout: The pre-deployment testing mode lets you check a zone or a delegation change before it goes live, by supplying future NS, glue and DS records on the command line. Keeping probe output as raw JSON separate from the analysis also means one probe can be re-graded or re-rendered later.
brief.status: unknown from the README alone. The README has no release dates or changelog. It lists current packaging in several distributions, a Docker image, and Python support through 3.12, and it notes that Python 2.7 support will be removed, which suggests ongoing upkeep. I did not check the release or commit history.
brief.caveats: Python 2.7 is still supported but is scheduled for removal. GOST algorithm support needs the OpenSSL GOST engine and M2Crypto, and cryptography alone cannot load that engine. Pre-deployment testing with zone files needs BIND, and the README warns about Debian AppArmor interference. Docker authoritative queries fail with EADDRNOTAVAIL unless you use --network host. RHEL and CentOS need extra repositories enabled first. The README's install instructions are mainly for Linux and do not describe Windows at all.
quotes: DNSViz is a tool suite for analysis and visualization of Domain Name System (DNS) behavior, including its security extensions (DNSSEC).
This tool suite powers the Web-based analysis available at https://dnsviz.net/
dnsviz probe takes one or more domain names as input and performs a series of queries to either recursive (default) or authoritative DNS servers, the results of which are serialized into JSON format.
A ready-to-use docker container is available for use.
